note: Amap (Alibaba) '高德途途' quadruped guide robot, debuted Apr 2026; official site says 'coming soon'. Specs only on WRC exhibitor listing (96-line LiDAR, Orin 250+ TOPS, 4 h), not filled.

name: Cheetah-Cub
summary: Small compliant research quadruped with spring-loaded pantographic legs and 8 servo actuators, built at EPFL BIOROB to study fast trotting.
note: Research platform (EPFL BIOROB, Spröwitz & Vespignani); tethered DC power, 8 Kondo servos.

name: SpaceBok
manufacturer: ESA / ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab

name: StarlETH
summary: ETH Zurich's first series-elastic-actuated quadruped (2011-2015), 3 DoF per leg, used to study locomotion control in the lab.
note: ETH Zurich Robotic Systems Lab page; research robot 2011-2015.

name: C1
compute_detail: x86 or domestic low-power ARM CPU
summary: Small industrial quadruped (15 kg, IP67) for patrol and inspection, with LiDAR navigation, autonomous charging and 8 kg payload.
note: Specs from Galileo (Tianjin) official product brochure (maker PDF hosted on WRC exhibitor site); product also listed on official site galileotimes.com. max_speed is stated limit (极限) speed; runtime range 3.5–6 h, upper value used; max payload 15 kg.

name: E1
compute_detail: x86 or domestic low-power ARM CPU
summary: Medium industrial quadruped (38 kg, IP67) with 20 kg payload, 4.95 m/s top speed and LiDAR navigation for security inspection.
note: Specs from Galileo (Tianjin) official product brochure (maker PDF hosted on WRC exhibitor site); product also listed on official site galileotimes.com. max_speed is stated limit (极限) speed; runtime range 2–4 h, upper value used; max payload 85 kg.

name: S1
compute_detail: x86 or domestic low-power ARM CPU
summary: Large industrial quadruped (60 kg, IP67) with 40 kg payload, 6 m/s top speed and up to 7.5 h runtime.
note: Specs from Galileo (Tianjin) official product brochure (maker PDF hosted on WRC exhibitor site); product also listed on official site galileotimes.com. max_speed is stated limit (极限) speed; runtime range 5 h (20 kg load) – 7.5 h, upper value used; max payload 120 kg.

name: Galileo X
summary: Multi-mode ground mobility platform combining AGV, off-road and legged capabilities; 200 kg rated load with 8 h full-load range.
note: Official Galileo news (2026 WRC launch, Aug 2026). Maker describes it as a ground-mobility platform merging AGV, off-road vehicle and quadruped forms (cruise/universal/global modes) — category 'Quadruped' may be better as Wheel-legged.

name: PARAM
summary: Rugged quadruped (0.6 m, 50 kg, 12 DoF, 25 kg payload) for inspection and payload delivery over rough ground.
note: Listed as 'Param' on official site ga.tech. HQ country not stated on official site (press says Bengaluru, India).

name: Gangben L1
compute_detail: 8-core CPU (EDU: NVIDIA Jetson Orin NX, 100 TOPS)
summary: Small 15 kg industrial quadruped with 12 self-developed joints, RL locomotion, IP54, 3.7 m/s and open SDK.
note: GENISOM AI (智身科技) official page, product 钢镚 L1. Limit speed 5 m/s; payload ≈8 kg (limit ~10 kg). Battery 43.2 V × 4.6 Ah rated (~199 Wh, computed; not stated as Wh). EDU version adds Jetson Orin NX, 3D LiDAR, depth camera.

name: Qiuqiu SP1
summary: Explosion-proof industrial quadruped for Zone 1/2 hazardous areas, 50 kg payload, IP66, for 24/7 autonomous inspection.
note: Official product name is 铅球 SP1 (Qianqiu/'shot put'), not 'Qiuqiu'. Explosion-proof inspection quadruped for Zone 1/2 gas atmospheres. Weight stated '≤100 kg'; runtime '≥4 h'.

name: Tongchui M1
compute_detail: 8-core CPU, 100 TOPS (Ultra: 128 TOPS)
summary: Mid-size industrial wheel-legged quadruped, 41 kg with 30 kg payload, IP67, 6 m/s, hot-swap dual batteries up to 5 h.
note: Official 铜锤 M1 (variants M1/Pro/Ultra): 12 joint motors + 4 hub motors (wheel-legged; optional point-foot kit), so category 'Quadruped' may be better as Wheel-legged. Limit speed 8 m/s. Battery 54 V × 9.35 Ah × 2 (~1010 Wh computed). Weight 41 kg with battery.

name: Lumen Q1
summary: All-terrain quadruped with 4D LiDAR for industrial inspection, logistics, security patrol and stage performance.
note: Maker is HECbot = Hubei Guanggu Dongzhi Embodied Intelligence (光谷东智), Wuhan. Specs (15 kg, 70x31x40 cm, 28-33.6 V, L1 4D LiDAR, 45 N·m) closely match Unitree Go2 — possibly a rebadged Go2 (inferred, not stated).

name: MQ01 Pro
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX (Ubuntu)
price_note: MANOÏD range priced EUR 30,000–150,000 depending on model/backpack (trade-press interview)
summary: Smallest MANOÏD quadruped for autonomous facility surveillance, with LiDAR, depth camera and ROS on Jetson Xavier NX.
note: Official datasheet name: 'MQ01 Pro LIDAR 2'. Maker MANOÏD (France).

name: MQ02
summary: IP66 all-terrain industrial quadruped for surveillance, inspection and mapping in hazardous or hard-to-reach environments.
note: Runtime is up to 2.5 h with two hot-swap batteries; continuous speed 3 m/s (5 m/s peak).

name: MQ03
summary: Ultra-robust IP67 industrial quadruped that climbs 45° stairs, compatible with SLAM and ROS/ROS2.
note: Available in Standard and PRO (GPS) versions; max user speed up to 5 m/s.

name: JINDO BOT
summary: Domestically produced full-autonomy quadruped from maum.ai for security patrol, defence and industrial safety, running on-device Physical AI.
note: maum.ai lists JINDO BOT on its Physical AI product line; it is a family brand with four mission variants (Guard, Ranger, Haechi, Vanguard). No official spec sheet found; pre-order/subscription stage.

name: Haoqizhe S01
summary: Small-to-medium industrial wheeled quadruped bringing MOVENEW P-series anti-magnetic/explosion/water/freeze protection to narrow spaces like pipe galleries.
note: Maker name should be MICBOT (Hangzhou Juwei Technology / 杭州具微科技), not 'MicroRoboTech'. Official name 好奇者 S01; wheeled quadruped launched at WAIC 2026. No spec table published.

name: MOVENEW P1
summary: Industrial wheel-legged quadruped for special operations in high-risk environments; 400 kg static and 200 kg walking load, 8–12 h runtime.
note: Maker is MICBOT (Hangzhou Juwei Technology). Wheel-legged quadruped (category arguably Wheel-legged). Datasheet says IP67 (wheels IP68) while feature text says IP66; datasheet value used. Explosion-proof variant P1 ExR exists.

name: MOVENEW P2
summary: Industrial special-purpose wheel-legged quadruped for high-risk complex conditions, with explosion-proof certification and ≥200 kg walking load.
note: Maker is MICBOT (Hangzhou Juwei Technology). Wheel-legged; Chinese-site datasheet nearly identical to P1 (77 kg, 3.2 kWh, 3 m/s) with dual 96-line LiDAR and IP67 body / IP68 wheels.

name: MOVENEW T1
sdk_name: Micbot Reinforcement Learning SDK / T1 SDK
compute_detail: 181 TOPS
summary: Flagship wheeled quadruped with 18 km/h top speed, 50 kg walking load and IP68 rating for high-end all-terrain work.
note: Maker is MICBOT (Hangzhou Juwei Technology). Wheel-legged flagship. Datasheet says IP68; feature blurb says IP66 — datasheet used. Speed 18 km/h = 5 m/s. Weight given as 40–50 kg range (left null).

name: Apollo
summary: Industrial IP67 quadruped for autonomous inspection with 50 kg walking payload, swappable battery and modular expansion.
note: Maker MirrorMe Technology (镜识科技), co-manufactured with Kaierda; peak 8 m/s record speed not on sold units.

name: MIT Cheetah
summary: MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab's first electric cheetah-sized quadruped, demonstrating energy-efficient running with high-torque-density motors.
note: Original electric MIT Cheetah (Cheetah 1). Research robot; 70 lb = 31.8 kg. Trotted 5 mph for up to 1.5 h in treadmill tests (test figure, not max speed).

name: MIT Cheetah 2
summary: Research quadruped for dynamic locomotion that runs up to 6.4 m/s and autonomously jumps over obstacles.
note: Archived project on MIT Biomimetic Robotics Lab site; runs 0–6.4 m/s, jumps 60 cm obstacles autonomously.

name: Cheetah 3
summary: Labrador-sized research quadruped that climbs debris-strewn stairs and recovers balance using blind, proprioceptive locomotion.
note: 90 lb = 40.8 kg per MIT MechE news. Designed for 'blind' locomotion without cameras.

name: Mini Cheetah
summary: Lightweight modular research quadruped with 12 low-cost actuators; first four-legged robot to perform a backflip.
note: 20 lb = 9.1 kg; 12 modular motors (3 per leg). Open software at github.com/mit-biomimetics/Cheetah-Software.

name: NEURA Quadruped
summary: Four-legged explorer robot for inspection, surveillance and payload transport over rough terrain and stairs, integrated with the Neuraverse.
note: Datasheet V1 (Jan 2026) says 'currently in development'; reservations open.

name: Bengpao Big Dog
summary: Hydraulic bionic quadruped ground vehicle for load carrying and following over rough mountain terrain; won the 2016 'Crossing the Obstacles' challenge.
note: Official name likely 'RUNNING' / 奔跑号 (mountain bionic quadruped platform); confirmed via IEEE ICUS 2017 paper authored by China North Vehicle Research Institute staff. Hydraulic research/demonstrator; maker site has no product page.

name: Solo 8
summary: Low-cost, open-source torque-controlled 8-DoF quadruped built from 3D-printed and off-the-shelf parts for legged-locomotion research.
note: Open-source 3D-printed research quadruped (NYU Tandon / MPI-IS). Weight 2.2 kg per v1 hardware README.

name: Simba
summary: Modular quadruped platform with sensor fusion and edge-AI computing for inspection, exploration and AI application development.
note: Pegatron shows a second-generation SIMBA II (COMPUTEX 2026, maxon HEJ 90 joints); first-gen Simba shown at COMPUTEX 2025. Official sources give no numeric specs.

name: RAIBO2
summary: Energy-efficient field quadruped with in-house actuators and RL control, running up to 6 m/s and walking about 8 hours per charge.
note: Developed by KAIST RaiLab (Prof. Hwangbo), commercialized by spin-off Raion Robotics. First quadruped to finish a full marathon (4:19:52). Weight/battery from developer's lab page and Nature preprint.

name: Explosion-Proof Quadruped Robot (SGZT-01)
summary: Sevnce's first-generation explosion-proof quadruped (SREX-SGZT-01), an electro-hydrostatic heavy-load inspection platform for oil, gas and chemical sites.
note: Maker launch release of 2 April 2024 (published with Sevnce as its source by OFweek, and repeated in the July 2025 review of the model line): whole-machine mass 149 kg, rated payload 200 kg, continuous working time 1.5 h, Ex IIB T4 Gb explosion protection, electro-hydrostatic drive. Sevnce's current site promotes the later X3 Stable and X5 and keeps no SGZT-01 page, so no dimension, DoF, IP rating or battery figure is filled; a distributor's page (100 kg / 30 kg / 1150 x 600 x 800 mm) is not a maker source and was not used. Superseded by X3 Stable and X5.

name: Explosion-Proof Four-Legged Robot X5
note: Sevnce (七腾机器人) X5 product page sevnce.com/detail?id=72 (checked 2026-11-17): all figures are stated as maxima - dimensions <=1200 x 750 x 950 mm, weight <=125 kg, payload 30 kg, straight-line speed <=2.0 m/s, 16+2 degrees of freedom, IP66, Ex IIB T4 Gb, -20 to +60 C, stairs <=20 cm high and >=25 cm deep, obstacle <=40 cm, wading <=15 cm, combined runtime >=2 h, charge <=3 h, laser SLAM + IMU with visual localisation, positioning <=5 cm. The page lists it as a wheel-leg hybrid, so the record's Quadruped category is the catalogue's own choice. Battery capacity is not published.

name: Baby Elephant
summary: Hydraulic quadruped with parallel-serial legs built at Shanghai Jiao Tong University as a heavy-load carrier for nuclear-plant maintenance and disaster relief.
note: From the Shanghai Jiao Tong University authors' own papers (ASME IDETC/CIE 2013 and the ASME Journal of Mechanisms and Robotics 2013): about 1 m tall, 1.2 m long, 0.5 m wide, about 130 kg, payload no less than 50 kg (a 2013 conference paper by the same group gives 60 kg), hydraulic actuation with three actuators per leg (12 in total, from the 2014 reaction-force paper) and a lithium battery in the belly; walks and trots outdoors by wireless remote control over 10 degree inclines. No speed, runtime or battery capacity is published.

name: Quadruped robot (DRDO technology demonstrator)
summary: Quadruped technology demonstrator built by Svaya Robotics with DRDO's R&DE (Pune) for reconnaissance and inspection in unstructured terrain for defence and security forces.
note: No maker product page exists. Svaya's own site (svayarobotics.com, checked 2026-11-17) presents only collaborative and humanoid robots and has no quadruped page; the robot is known from the company's March 2023 release, reported by The Hindu, that it was developed with DRDO labs R&DE and DEBEL as a technology demonstrator with design inputs from R&DE, for remote reconnaissance and inspection where it is unsafe for people to operate. No mass, dimension, speed, payload or battery figure has been published by Svaya, so every spec field stays empty.

name: Jamoca
summary: Research quadruped from Tencent Robotics X that walks Kung-Fu plum-blossom piles using its own perception, planning and 1 kHz torque control; the body is an externally supplied platform.
note: Tencent's own announcement of 20 November 2020: Jamoca is built on an externally supplied body, weighs about 70 kg, is 1 m long, 0.5 m wide and 0.75 m tall, walks, trots and jumps, and localises to within 1 cm with 10 ms replanning and 1 kHz torque control. One Tencent report gives 1.5 m for the length while the same announcement's figures give 1 m; the shorter figure is recorded. Tencent publishes no speed, payload, DoF (12 is usually assumed for this body), battery or IP figure; it is used for internal lab experiments only.

name: TITAN-XIII
summary: Lightweight sprawling-type quadruped built by the Hirose/Endo laboratory at Tokyo Institute of Technology with wire-driven legs, used to demonstrate fast, energy-efficient dynamic walking.
note: Figures are from the laboratory's own publications - ROBOMECH Journal 2016 (Kitano, Hirose, Horigome, Endo) and IROS 2013: standard posture 220 x 550 x 300 mm, 5.65 kg including the LiFePO4 battery (26.4 V, 1100 mAh), 12 DoF (3 per leg), maximum walking speed 1.38 m/s at COT 1.76, and a 5 kg walking payload (20 kg when statically supported). Published size differs between papers - 420 x 420 x 300 mm in the IROS 2013 table and 600 x 600 x 300 mm in the ROBOMECH 2013 table - and the ROBOMECH 2013 table lists 1.0 m/s and a 1 kg payload, so the 2016 journal values are recorded here. Battery Wh is not stated by the maker.

name: Xingzai
summary: Topstar's (拓斯达) first quadruped, launched 16 January 2026 at Songshan Lake for industrial inspection, forest firefighting and security patrols.
note: Topstar product page (checked 2026-11-17) and its launch item of 16 January 2026: 8 h endurance, 5 m/s, 20 km per mission, obstacles and stairs over 20 cm, 45 degree inner slope, 200 kg static load and 80 kg walking load (80 kg recorded), IP66, -20 to 55 C, expandable with night-vision, dual-light gimbal, partial-discharge tester or an arm. The maker publishes no mass, dimensions, DoF, battery or price.

name: Laikago
summary: Unitree's first quadruped, an all-electric research platform from 2017 named after the space dog Laika and later replaced by the Aliengo and Go series.
note: Unitree no longer carries a Laikago page (unitree.com/laikago returns 404, checked 2026-11-17). The figures recorded are the maker's own: the launch video on Unitree's channel gives 22 kg and 0.56 x 0.35 x 0.6 m standing, and Unitree's laikago_ros model has 12 revolute joints (3 per leg). Unitree never published a full Laikago datasheet - the 2020 page had an empty parameters section - so speed, payload, runtime and battery capacity stay empty rather than taking press figures (0.8 m/s and 7 kg appear in press coverage only). A later 2019 revision was listed at 24 kg.

name: AlphaDog C500
compute_detail: ARM 64-bit CPU, 32 GB storage, Linux + ROS
summary: Fifth-generation AlphaDog C-series quadruped developer robot (standard version) with Linux/ROS, AI voice and vision.
note: Official C-series spec table (C500 'Standard developer version'). Speed 'up to 1.5 m/s' (max safe speed 3.0 m/s stated separately). Size 76x40x45 cm standing; runtime = 'average up to 5.7 h'; battery 23 Ah lithium (Wh not stated).

name: AlphaDog C501
compute_detail: ARM 64-bit CPU, 32 GB storage, Linux + ROS
summary: Top C-series AlphaDog developer quadruped adding depth vision, visual mapping and autonomous navigation; Linux/ROS.
note: Official C-series spec table (C501 'Ultimate developer version'): adds depth camera, visual mapping and autonomous navigation over C500. Speed up to 1.5 m/s (max safe 3.0 m/s).

name: AlphaDog E300
note: WEILAN's AlphaDog E-Series page (alphadoge.html, read 2026-11-17) carries a 'Reference Specifications' table for the E300: speed up to 3 m/s, adjustable walking height 18-37 cm, adjustable width 20-32 cm, gradeability up to 20 degrees, payload up to 5 kg, V-SLAM, autonomous navigation and dynamic balancing. The maker publishes no mass, length, runtime, DoF or battery capacity for the E300, so those stay empty; third-party figures (13 kg, 3 h) are not used.

name: AlphaDog E400L
note: WEILAN's AlphaDog E-Series page (read 2026-11-17) 'Reference Specifications' table for the E400L: speed up to 4 m/s, adjustable walking height 25-50 cm, width 20-32 cm, gradeability up to 20 degrees, payload up to 10 kg, V-SLAM, autonomous navigation and dynamic balancing. The maker publishes no mass, length, runtime, DoF or battery capacity, so those fields stay empty; third-party figures (18 kg, 5 h, USD 27,690) are not used.

name: BabyAlpha A2
summary: Consumer AI companion robot dog with LLM chat, face recognition, home patrol, auto-charging and remote video calls.
note: Official CN page lists four trims: A2 (CNY 8,599, 3.6 km/h, ~60 min), Plus, Pro, Ultra (CNY 25,599, 7.2 km/h, ~120 min). Values below are base A2. 12 actuators stated.

name: Tianlang Q25
summary: Industrial all-terrain quadruped rated -40 to 55 °C with a flat payload deck for public safety, defense and logistics.
note: Official 天狼 Q25 page (58znkj.com/tianlang). Payload = continuous walking load ~25 kg. IP 'not lower than IP65'.

name: CyberDog (1st generation)
compute_detail: NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX (21 TOPS), 128 GB SSD
summary: Xiaomi's first open-source bio-inspired quadruped for developers, with in-house servos, Jetson Xavier NX and SLAM navigation.
note: Official mi.com CyberDog page: max walking speed 3.2 m/s is lab-tested (max safe speed 1.6 m/s). 11 sensors. Dimensions/weight are on mi.com/cyberdog/specs but rendered as images, not machine-readable; left null. Launch price RMB 9,999 per Xiaomi community post (1,000 units).

name: Svan M2
summary: xTerra Robotics' small Indian quadruped for industrial inspection, research and security patrols, driven by quasi-direct-drive actuators and controlled over ROS.
note: xTerra SVAN M2 product page (checked 2026-11-17): 11 kg, payload about 5 kg, 41.2 x 40 x 41.2 cm, 12 actuated DoF with QDD A2 actuators, max speed 1.0 m/s, 240 Wh lithium-polymer battery, Raspberry Pi 4B 8 GB, ROS, -5 to 40 C, 2.4 GHz WiFi. The maker's documentation site for the same robot gives 15 kg, 1.5 m/s and 2-4 h battery life, and describes ROS 2 support; the product page figures are recorded and the difference is noted here.

name: e-Dog
summary: Small servo-driven robot dog from Yobotics for education, voice interaction and secondary development, sold with an open Android and STM32 control stack.
note: Yobotics quadruped page (checked 2026-11-17), e-Dog table: 390 x 230 x 240 mm, 2.5 kg, 1 kg payload, 2.5 h, 0.67 m/s, 10 degree climb, PC+ABS shell, 13 DoF, high-torque servos, phone-app and voice control, Android (quad-core Cortex-A7) plus STM32 motion control, ultrasonic/infrared/vision/attitude/voice sensors, 8.4 V 2 A adapter. The maker's tab labels on that page are shifted by one section, but the table under the e-Dog entry names the model itself.

name: Y10
summary: Mid-size lightweight high-dynamics quadruped from Yobotics for research, with 144 N.m peak actuators and a CAN-bus, Linux-based controller.
note: Yobotics quadruped page (checked 2026-11-17), Y10 table: about 980 x 510 x 500 mm, about 37 kg, load >=15 kg, speed >=4 m/s, slope >=30 degrees, runtime >=70 min (1 h recorded as the lower bound), 12 DoF (3 per leg), aluminium body, quasi-direct-drive planetary reduction, peak torque about 144 N.m, Intel Atom core board, CAN bus, 1 kHz feedback control, Linux, Yobotics IMU. The page also lists a CNY 43,300 price.

name: Y20
summary: Yobotics all-terrain inspection quadruped positioned between the Y10 research platform and the Y30 outdoor flagship.
note: Yobotics lists Y20 in its quadruped catalogue navigation and announced the wheeled Y20-W on 18 September 2025, but the published parameter table for Y20 is an image on the maker's category page and no text specification was obtained; the maker's news list carries no Y20 specification item. With no maker figure to cite, no field is filled and the record stays unconfirmed.

name: Y30
summary: Yobotics' all-terrain outdoor flagship quadruped for inspection, load carrying and work in hazardous environments.
note: Yobotics quadruped page (checked 2026-11-17), Y30 table: standing about 1100 x 475 x 610 mm, folded 930 x 450 x 370 mm, about 60 kg with battery, battery 25 Ah (Wh not stated), >5 h continuous walking without load and >2.5 h with a working load, standing load up to 150 kg and walking load up to 80 kg (80 kg recorded), max 4 m/s, IP54, 40 degree stairs and 40 degree slopes, 30 cm step height, -25 to +50 C, Intel Atom x5-Z8350 controller; 3D LiDAR and depth camera optional. DoF is not stated on the page.

name: YJ30
note: Yuejia Lingdong YJ30 page (checked 2026-11-17) and the maker's bilingual brochure: standing 682 x 354 x 462 mm, 17.5 kg, payload 10 kg, 1.5-2 h (3 h with a second battery), 20 cm stair, 3 m/s, 50 deg climb, IP54, WiFi/4G/5G, video transmission, ASR and follow/navigation. Price CNY 88,000 on the maker's page. The table merges climb angle and DoF under one heading and gives only 50 deg, so dof stays empty; no battery capacity is published.

name: Lingmao Cyvet
summary: Uniubi AI's (宇泛智能) 15 kg quadruped developer platform with optional NVIDIA Jetson Orin compute, sold for embodied-AI research and developer projects.
note: Uniubi AI product page (checked 2026-11-17): standing 672 x 355 x 432 mm (crouched 718 x 410 x 178 mm), about 15 kg with battery, payload about 20 kg, 0-3 m/s, up to 5.5 h unloaded and about 3.5 h with 15 kg, 432 Wh (10000 mAh) battery, 12 self-developed joints (60 N.m peak), 17 cm continuous stairs, -10 to 50 C, binocular camera, IMU, microphone and speaker standard with LiDAR and 360 degree UWB optional, Orin Nano/NX up to 157 TOPS optional, C++/Python SDK. Standard version is indoor/dry-outdoor only; IP54 applies to an industrial customized version, so ip_rating stays empty.

name: Prahasta
summary: Zen Technologies' four-legged robot for counter-insurgency and close-quarter defence work, using LiDAR and reinforcement learning and carrying 9 mm, 5.56 mm or 7.62 mm small arms.
note: Zen's own Prahasta page (checked 2026-11-17) describes the robot and its weapon compatibility but publishes no numeric specification at all - no mass, dimensions, speed, payload, runtime or battery. Press coverage of the July 2024 launch gives 2.5 h with a 45 kg load, an 80 kg lift and obstacles of about 40 cm, but those figures are press-only, so no field is filled.
